questions.q:
For a society to develop, its attitude towards life must not be a fatalistic one; rather, it must have strong faith in its capacity to improve.

The sentence best supports the statement that _________.
options: the attitude of a society towards life is indicative of its socio-economic development
success in life starts from one's dissatisfaction with the existing state of affairs
a society cannot progress unless it is actively committed to the pursuit of a better life
a person develops a healthy attitude towards life through constant efforts to improve oneself
a person with an optimistic outlook in life is confident of his capacity for advancement
questions.answer: a person with an optimistic outlook in life is confident of his capacity for advancement

questions.q:
Freedom and human rights without food are like freeing a prisoner and then not giving the prisoner the key to get out of the cell. The 450 million people who today live in the shadow of hunger and death from malnutrition can never be free men and women, however entrenched their freedom may be. These freedoms are only prospects held out and not realized.

The paragraph best supports the statement that __________.
options: at times people have to work as one nation to address the problem of malnutrition
most of the poor countries in the world today still depend on "super" rich countries for support
the satisfaction of one's basic needs is a prerequisite to the enjoyment of freedom
a country which cannot feed its people with its own resources could never be free
a country could not be free unless it could prove to the world that it could stand on its own feet
questions.answer: the satisfaction of one's basic needs is a prerequisite to the enjoyment of freedom

questions.q:
The Einstein revolution has produced a paradox; while vastly extending humankind's reach, it has also exposed the essentially finite nature of the human scale.

The sentence best supports the statement that Einstein's discovery _________.
options: proclaims only the glory of the universe
involves a real but not obvious contradiction
reveals a contradiction between God and his people
questions.answer: involves a real but not obvious contradiction

questions.q:
A little ignorance when launching economic development projects may be a fruitful stimulus to ingenious new approaches.

The sentence best supports the statement that __________.
options: new techniques insure success of development plans
new approaches bring about change and success
ignorance sometimes gives birth to new knowledge
lack of knowledge in economic ventures may lead to better and improved results
questions.answer: new approaches bring about change and success

questions.q:
If legislation is to change social attitudes and values, it must come with adequate enforcement and machinery, which should include efforts to educate people on these laws. Otherwise, legal provisions not only remain dead letters, but actually promote lack of respect for the law.

The paragraph best supports the statement that __________.
options: people should respect laws because laws protect them
the effectiveness of laws lies in adequate education of the people about them and their proper enforcement.
laws lose their effectiveness if people do not respect them
ignorance of the law does not excuse anyone
laws could change the social attitudes and values of people if properly enforced
questions.answer: the effectiveness of laws lies in adequate education of the people about them and their proper enforcement.

questions.q:
Two persons look out through the same bars; one sees mud and the other, the stars.

The sentence best supports the statement that __________.
options: some people are more blind than others
people see things differently depending on their own perspective
people have varied ways of looking at different things
people have different tastes and interests
people tend to influence one another's views of things
questions.answer: people see things differently depending on their own perspective

questions.q:
An education really suited to the rural environment can become both acceptable and genuinely functional only when the environment begins to offer real opportunities and to require skills and knowledge on a large scale. As long as opportunities lie only in the urban economy, education will remain in servitude to that small section of society.

The paragraph best supports the statement that __________.
options: migration to the cities results from the lack of real opportunities in the rural areas
the rural environment has opportunities that need to be developed
we have a concentration of educational opportunities in the urban areas
rural occupational opportunities give meaning to rural education
our educational system caters mainly to the needs of the urban sector
questions.answer: rural occupational opportunities give meaning to rural education

questions.q:
No matter how strong and dedicated leaders may be, they must find root and strength among the people. Alone, they cannot save a nation. They may guide, they may set the tone, they may dedicate themselves and risk their lives, but ultimately national survival lies in the people.

The paragraph best supports the statement that __________.
options: dedication and the right sense of direction enable a leader to guide the people
good leadership is essential to effective public administration
it is the leader who determines the fate of a nation
the people of a nation shape their own destiny with the guidance of a leader
the strength of the people comes from a dynamic and forceful leader
questions.answer: the people of a nation shape their own destiny with the guidance of a leader

questions.q:
Ang pagbaba ng halaga ng piso ay lumikha ng krisis sa maraming industriya ng bansa. Kasunod nito ang pagtitipid at problema sa kawalan ng mapasukang trabaho. Lumikha rin ito ng pagtataas ng presyo ng mga bilihin na labis na nakaapekto sa kita ng mga manggagawa.

Ayon sa talata __________.
options: ang kasalukuyang krisis ay bunga ng mga mahal na bilihin at kawalan ng mapasukang trabaho
ang krisis ay nakaapekto sa hangarin ng maraming industriya na makapagbigay ng karagdagang sahod sa kanilang mga manggagawa
dumarami ang mga walang hanapbuhay at tumataas ang halaga ng mga bilihin dahil sa krisis
maraming industriya ang nalulugi dahil sa krisis kaya itinataas din nila ang presyo ng kanilang mga produkto.
dahil sa krisis, maraming industriya ang napilitang magsara
questions.answer: dumarami ang mga walang hanapbuhay at tumataas ang halaga ng mga bilihin dahil sa krisis

questions.q:
The gregariousness of people is mostly due to a fear of remaining alone. It feels safer to be with a group, talk like a group, act like a group. The ramparts of group solidarity give the members security.

The paragraph best supports the statement that __________.
options: people who belong to a group react to situations in the same manner
some people are more gregarious than others
people who are gregarious are afraid to be alone

questions.q:
Most researches in needy countries are based on the thinking and approach of the highly developed Western world, and seldom have they been directed toward meeting the countries' own development needs.

The sentence best supports the statement that _________.
options: highly developed countries offer the best guide for the development of needy countries
most researches done in needy countries are missing their objectives
needy countries need researchers to help them reach the status of the western world
needy countries spend so much time for conducting researches
questions.answer: most researches done in needy countries are missing their objectives

questions.q:
In a modern economy, the results of long-range planning frequently depend upon the future value of money. The ability then to predict the value of money is a key to economic progress.

The paragraph best supports the statement that _________.
options: the value of money is unpredictable at times
the unpredictability of money is an obstacle to a nation's prosperity
economic progress is facilitated by properly controlling budgetary expenses
long-range planning is unheard of in traditional economies
financial planning is indispensable in modern economy
questions.answer: financial planning is indispensable in modern economy

questions.q:
Sixty years ago I knew everything; now I know nothing; education is a progressive discovery of our own ignorance.

The sentence best supports the statement that __________.
options: the older we get, the more we forget what we have learned
the older we get, the more knowledgeable we become
the more we learn, the more we realize that there's more we need to know
we learn more as we grow old
questions.answer: the more we learn, the more we realize that there's more we need to know

questions.q:
Nagawang mabago ng mga kasalukuyang awitin ang kamalayan ng Pilipino upang kantahin ang sarili niyang mga awit sa tanging wikang nakapagsasatinig sa kanyang kaluluwa.

Isinasaad ng pangungusap na __________.
options: madamdamin at makabuluhan ang mga awiting isinulat sa wikang Pilipino
tagumpay ang mga awiting Pilipino na mabago ang kaugalian ng mga taong Pilipino
madaling matutuhan ang mga awiting Pilipino dahil ang mga ito ay nasusulat sa katutubong wika
natututuhan nang tangkilikin ng mga Pilipino ang kanilang mga sariling awitin
nagkakaroon na ng kamalayan ang mga Pilipino tungkol sa lahat ng mga awitin ngayon
questions.answer: natututuhan nang tangkilikin ng mga Pilipino ang kanilang mga sariling awitin

questions.q:
Chang-Rae Lee's award-winning debut novel "Native Speaker" is about Henry Park, a Korean-American individual who struggles to find his place as an immigrant in a suburb of New York City. This novel addresses the notion that as the individuals who know us best, our family, peers, and lovers are the individuals who direct our lives and end up defining us. Henry Park is confronted with this reality in the very beginning of the novel, which opens: "The day my wife left she gave me a list of who I was." Upon separating from his wife, Park struggles with racial and ethnic identity issues due to his loneliness. Through Park's work as an undercover operative for a private intelligence agency, the author presents the theme of espionage as a metaphor for the internal divide that Park experiences as an immigrant.

Chang-Rae Lee is also a first-generation Korean-American immigrant. Themes of identity, race, and cultural alienation pervade his works. In his works and through his characters, Lee shows us both the difficulties and the subtleties of the immigrant experience in America.

Which of the following best describes the purpose of this passage?

Chang-Rae Lee's award-winning debut novel "Native Speaker" is about Henry Park, a Korean-American individual who struggles to find his place as an immigrant in a suburb of New York City. This novel addresses the notion that as the individuals who know us best, our family, peers, and lovers are the individuals who direct our lives and end up defining us. Henry Park is confronted with this reality in the very beginning of the novel, which opens: "The day my wife left she gave me a list of who I was." Upon separating from his wife, Park struggles with racial and ethnic identity issues due to his loneliness.

Why does the author of the passage quote the first line of the novel "Native Speaker"?
options: To illustrate one of the themes in the novel.
To show how the book is semi-autobiographical.
It is the main idea of the novel.
To create interest in the novel.
questions.answer: To illustrate one of the themes in the novel.

questions.q:
Perimenopause is the time leading up to menopause, an interval when menopause-related changes begin to be noticed. Most women experience the first signs of perimenopause around the age of forty. Symptoms experienced during perimenopause include headaches, depression and anxiety, hot flashes and night sweats, insomnia and fatigue, urinary problems and vaginal dryness, weight gain, heart palpitations, and loss of bone mass. Perimenopause usually takes place between the ages of 45 and 55. The symptoms of perimenopause are a normal manifestation of the aging process and do not ordinarily require treatment.

The purpose of this article is to...
options: Enumerate the symptoms that women may experience when going through perimenopause.
Give an overall description of perimenopause.
questions.answer: Give an overall description of perimenopause.

questions.q:
The United States has always been a pluralistic society, meaning it has embraced many points of view and many groups with different identities from its beginning. The first political parties developed in the United States as a result of conflicting visions of the American identity. The event that brought this disagreement to the surface was the creation of the Bank of the United States in 1791. The Democratic-Republican Party developed to protest the bank, while the Federalist Party was established in defense of the bank. These different points of view—central government versus separate states—would not be resolved easily.

What is the author's purpose in writing this passage?
options: To persuade the reader to accept the Federalist Party's point of view.
To explain the disagreements between early American political parties.
To explain the importance of a strong central government.
To criticize the founders of the Bank of the United States.
questions.answer: To explain the disagreements between early American political parties.

questions.q:
Current statistics indicate that between 16 and 20 percent of a school's population suffer from a psychological condition known as oppositional defiant disorder, or ODD. ODD symptoms include difficulty complying with adult requests, excessive arguments with adults, temper tantrums, difficulty accepting responsibility for actions, low frustration tolerance, and behaviors intended to annoy or upset adults. Unfortunately, ODD can be caused by a number of factors. Various types of therapy are helpful in treating ODD, and some drugs can treat particular symptoms. However, no single cure exists. The best advice from professionals is directed toward parents.

The author's purpose in writing this passage is to...
options: Prove that parents are the cause of ODD.
Inform the reader about this complex condition.
Persuade the reader to keep students with ODD out of public school.
questions.answer: Inform the reader about this complex condition.

questions.q:
It is tempting to think that your eyes are simply mirrors that reflect whatever is in front of them. Researchers, however, have shown that your brain is constantly working to create the impression of a continuous, uninterrupted world. For instance, in the last 10 minutes, you have blinked your eyes around 200 times, yet you have probably not been aware of any of these interruptions. Nor are you aware of the artery that runs right down the middle of your retina, creating a large blind spot in your visual field. Your brain works hard to make the world look continuous!

What is the main purpose of this passage?
options: To persuade the reader to pay close attention to blind spots.
To explain the way visual perception works.
To persuade the reader to consult an optometrist if the O and X disappear.
To prove that vision is a passive process.
questions.answer: To explain the way visual perception works.

questions.q:
Grapes are one of the oldest cultivated fruits. Grapes have been grown in California for more than 200 years. The tradition of viticulture began in 1769 when Spanish friars established missions throughout California. William Wolfskill planted the first table grape vineyard in 1839 near Los Angeles. By the 1850s, the United States had officially acquired California from Mexico, and 80,000 gold prospectors had moved to the region. Today, California wine, table grapes, and raisins are all important agricultural commodities, with approximately 700,000 acres planted in vineyards.

The author most likely wrote this passage to...

Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks support a wide diversity of animal species, reflecting the range in elevation, climate, and habitat variety there. Over 260 native vertebrate species are in the parks; numerous additional species may be present but have not been confirmed. Many of the parks' caves contain invertebrates, some of which exist only in one cave and are known nowhere else in the world. Local species include the gray fox, bobcat, striped and spotted skunks, black bear, wood rat, pocket gopher, white-footed mouse, California quail, scrub jay, lesser goldfinch, wrentit, acorn woodpecker, gopher snake, California king snake, striped racer, western whiptail lizard, and the California newt.

What was the author's purpose in writing this passage?

Black History Month is unnecessary. In a place and time in which we overwhelmingly elected an African-American president, we can and should move to a post-racial approach to education. In addition to being unnecessary, the idea that African-American history should be focused on in a given month suggests that it belongs in that month alone. Instead, it is important to incorporate African-American history into what is taught every day as American history. There are a number of other reasons to abolish it: it has become a shallow commercial ritual, there is a paternalistic flavor to it, and it suggests the knowledge imparted in that month is for African-Americans only.

The author's primary purpose in this passage is to...
options: Argue that Black History Month should not be so commercial.
Argue that Black History Month should be abolished.
Argue that Black History Month should be maintained.
Suggest that African-American history should be taught in two months rather than just one.
Argue that African-American history is not part of mainstream curriculum.
questions.answer: Argue that Black History Month should be abolished.

questions.q:
In the 16th century, an age of great marine and terrestrial exploration, Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail around the world. As a young Portuguese noble, he served the king of Portugal, but he became involved in the quagmire of political intrigue at court and lost the king's favor.

The 16th century was an age of great ______ exploration.

In the 16th century, Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to sail around the world. As a young Portuguese noble, he served the king of Portugal, but he became involved in the quagmire of political intrigue at court and lost the king's favor.

Magellan lost the favor of the king of Portugal when he became involved in a political ________.

A papal decree of 1493 had assigned all land in the New World west of 50 degrees W longitude to Spain and all the land east of that line to Portugal.

The Pope divided New World lands between Spain and Portugal according to their location on one side or the other of an imaginary geographical line 50 degrees west of Greenwich that extends in a _________ direction.

On September 20, 1519, Magellan set sail from Spain with five ships. More than a year later, one of these ships was exploring the topography of South America in search of a water route across the continent.

One of Magellan's ships explored the _________ of South America for a passage across the continent.

This ship sank, but the remaining four ships searched along the southern peninsula of South America.

Four of the ships sought a passage along a southern ______.
options: body of land with water on three sides
questions.answer: body of land with water on three sides

questions.q:
Finally they found the passage they sought near 50 degrees S latitude. Magellan named this passage the Strait of All Saints, but today it is known as the Strait of Magellan.

The passage was found near 50 degrees S of ________.

Those who remained crossed the meridian now known as the International Date Line in the early spring of 1521 after 98 days on the Pacific Ocean.

In the spring of 1521, the ships crossed the _______ now called the International Date Line.
options: imaginary circle passing through the poles
imaginary line parallel to the equator
questions.answer: imaginary circle passing through the poles

questions.q:
Marie Curie was one of the most accomplished scientists in history. Together with her husband, Pierre, she discovered radium, an element widely used for treating cancer, and studied uranium and other radioactive substances. Pierre and Marie's amicable collaboration later helped to unlock the secrets of the atom.

The Curies' _________ collaboration helped to unlock the secrets of the atom.

Marie was born in 1867 in Warsaw, Poland, where her father was a professor of physics. At an early age, she displayed a brilliant mind and a blithe personality.

Marie had a bright mind and a ______ personality.

Her great exuberance for learning prompted her to continue with her studies after high school. She became disgruntled, however, when she learned that the university in Warsaw was closed to women.

When she learned that she could not attend the university in Warsaw, she felt _________.

She became disgruntled, however, when she learned that the university in Warsaw was closed to women. Determined to receive a higher education, she defiantly left Poland and in 1891 entered the Sorbonne, a French university, where she earned her master's degree and doctorate in physics.

Marie _________ by leaving Poland and traveling to France to enter the Sorbonne.

A short time after they discovered radium, Pierre was killed by a horse-drawn wagon in 1906. Marie was stunned by this horrible misfortune and endured heartbreaking anguish. Despondently she recalled their close relationship and the joy that they had shared in scientific research.

_________ she remembered their joy together.

Curie's feeling of desolation finally began to fade when she was asked to succeed her husband as a physics professor at the Sorbonne.

Her _________ began to fade when she returned to the Sorbonne to succeed her husband.

Although Marie Curie eventually suffered a fatal illness from her long exposure to radium, she never became disillusioned about her work.

Even though she became fatally ill from working with radium, Marie Curie was never _________.

Early the next morning, Mount Vesuvius poured a huge river of molten rock down upon Herculaneum, completely burying the city and filling the harbor with coagulated lava.

Herculaneum and its harbor were buried under _________ lava.

Poisonous sulfuric gases saturated the air. These heavy gases were not buoyant in the atmosphere and therefore sank toward the earth and suffocated people.

The poisonous gases were not _________ in the air.

Over the years, excavations of Pompeii and Herculaneum have revealed a great deal about the behavior of the volcano. By analyzing data, much as a zoologist dissects an animal specimen, scientists have concluded that the eruption changed large portions of the area's geography.

Scientists analyzed data about Vesuvius in the same way that a zoologist _________ a specimen.

Meteorologists studying these events have also concluded that Vesuvius caused a huge tidal wave that affected the world's climate.

_________ have concluded that the volcanic eruption caused a tidal wave.

In addition to making these investigations, archaeologists have been able to study the skeletons of victims by using distilled water to wash away the volcanic ash.

Scientists have used _________ water to wash away volcanic ash from the skeletons of victims.

Elizabeth I, Queen of England, encouraged her staunch admiral of the navy, Sir Francis Drake, to raid Spanish ships and towns. Though these raids were on a small scale, Drake achieved dramatic success, adding gold and silver to England's treasury and diminishing Spain's supremacy.

Sir Francis Drake added wealth to the treasury and diminished Spain's _________.

Philip intended his fleet to be indestructible. In addition to building new warships, he marshaled 130 sailing vessels of all types and recruited more than 19,000 robust soldiers and 8,000 sailors.

King Philip recruited many ______ soldiers and sailors.

The martial Armada set sail from Lisbon, Portugal, on May 9, 1588, but bad weather forced it back to port.

The ______ Armada set sail on May 9, 1588.

The Spanish fleet met the smaller, faster, and more maneuverable English ships in battle off the coast of Plymouth, England, first on July 31 and again on August 2. The two battles left Spain vulnerable, having lost several ships and with its ammunition depleted.

The two battles left the Spanish fleet _________.

On August 7, while the Armada lay at anchor on the French side of the Strait of Dover, England sent eight burning ships into the midst of the Spanish fleet to set it on fire. Blocked on one side, the Spanish ships could only drift away, their crews in panic and disorder.

The Armada was ______ on one side.
options: Answer not available in this article

questions.q:
Darius, king of the Persian Empire, was furious because Athens had interceded for the other Greek city-states in revolt against Persian domination.

Athens had _________ the other Greek city-states against the Persians.
options: given orders for all to fight

questions.q:
In anger the king sent an enormous army to defeat Athens. He thought it would take drastic steps to pacify the rebellious part of the empire.

Darius took drastic steps to ________ the rebellious Athenians.

Persia was ruled by one man. In Athens, however, all citizens helped to rule. Ennobled by this participation, Athenians were prepared to die for their city-state.

Their participation _________ to the Athenians.

The frightened citizens of Delos refused to believe this. Not wanting to abet the conquest of Greece, they fled from their city and did not return until the Persians had left.

The people of Delos did not want to ______ the conquest of Greece.

The Athenians refurbished their weapons and moved to the plain of Marathon, where their little band would meet the Persians. At the last moment, soldiers from Plataea reinforced the Athenian troops.

The Athenians were _________ by some soldiers who arrived from Plataea.

All of the gods and goddesses had been invited to the wedding celebration in Troy except Eris, goddess of discord. She had been omitted from the guest list because her presence always embroiled mortals and immortals alike in conflict.

Eris was known for _________ both mortals and immortals.

The job eventually fell to Paris, son of King Priam of Troy, who was said to be a good judge of beauty. Paris did not have an easy job. Each goddess, eager to win the golden apple, tried aggressively to bribe him.

Each goddess tried ______ to bribe Paris.

"I'll grant you vast kingdoms to rule," promised Hera. "Vast kingdoms are nothing in comparison with my gift," contradicted Athena. "Choose me and I'll see that you win victory and fame in war."

Athena _________ Hera, promising Paris victory and fame in war.

During his reign over Russia, the czar had planned to revoke many of the harsh laws established by previous czars. Some workers and peasants, however, clamored for more rapid social reform.

Some Russian peasants and workers ______ for social reform.

Although witnesses vouched that all the members of the czar's family had been executed, there were rumors suggesting that Anastasia had survived.

Witnesses ______ that all members of the czar's family had been executed.

The doctors and nurses thought that she resembled Anastasia and questioned her about her background. She disclaimed any connection with the czar's family.

Tschaikovsky initially ______ any connection with the czar's family.

She had married one of the brothers, who had taken her to Berlin and left her there, penniless and without a vocation. Unable to invoke the aid of her mother's family in Germany, she had tried to drown herself.

She was unable to ______ the aid of her relatives.

She returned to Germany in 1933 to bring suit against her mother's family. There she declaimed to the court, asserting that she was indeed Anastasia and deserved her inheritance.

In court she _________ maintaining that she was Anastasia and deserved her inheritance.

While French citizens begged for lower taxes, the queen embellished her palace with extravagant works of art. She also surrounded herself with artists, writers, and musicians, who encouraged the queen to spend money even more profusely.

The people surrounding the queen encouraged her to spend money ______.

These high taxes paid for the entertainments the queen and her court so enjoyed. When the minister of finance tried to stop these royal spendthrifts, the queen replaced him.

The minister of finance tried to curb these royal ______.

Although many people who heard about the first powered flight on December 17, 1903 were excited and impressed, others reacted with peals of laughter. The idea of flying an aircraft was repulsive to some people.

The idea of flying an aircraft was ______ to some people.

The idea of flying an aircraft was repulsive to some people. Such people called Wilbur and Orville Wright, the inventors of the first flying machine, impulsive fools.

People thought that the Wright brothers had ______.

In 1896, when they read about the death of Otto Lilienthal, the brothers' interest in flight grew into a compulsion.

The Wrights' interest in flight grew into a ______.

Lilienthal, a pioneer in hang-gliding, had controlled his gliders by shifting his body in the desired direction. This idea was repellent to the Wright brothers, however, and they searched for more efficient methods to control the balance of airborne vehicles.

Lilienthal's idea about controlling airborne vehicles was _________ the Wrights.

Because of their efforts, the old tables were repealed in time and replaced by the first reliable figures for air pressure on curved surfaces.

The old tables were _________ and replaced by the first reliable figures for air pressure on curved surfaces.

In 1903 the Wrights built their first airplane, which cost less than $1,000. They even designed and built their own source of propulsion—a lightweight gasoline engine.

The Wrights designed and built their own source of _________.
